key_insight: HAD-VLM combines text generation with continuous numerical prediction to better align medical vision-language models with ultrasound measurement tasks. Instead of treating every measurement as discrete text tokens, it uses a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework.
problem_solved: Quantitative ultrasound requires continuous measurements, but conventional vision-language models predict numbers as discrete tokens, creating a mismatch between the prediction format and the measurement target.
method: Use a shared backbone for autoregressive text generation and continuous measurement prediction.
Combine autoregressive and diffusion modeling for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement.
Adapt the vision encoder to ultrasound images through visual prompt tuning.
impact: The approach offers practitioners a way to combine language interaction with continuous-valued medical predictions. The provided abstract is truncated, so performance gains and clinical validation cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side illustration of discrete number tokens versus a continuous measurement scale.
Architecture diagram showing an ultrasound image and prompt entering a shared backbone with text and measurement outputs.
Ultrasound image with an illustrative measurement line and numerical label.
Visual prompt tuning diagram highlighting adaptation of the vision encoder to ultrasound.
paper_title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Dianye Huang, Jiamei Guo, Yue Zhou, Mingde Li, Yi Xiong
